misconception_description: Student believes that while loops execute their body only once if the condition is true.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungKemunculanStd
kamus
  s : string
  i, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(s)
  jumlah <- 0
  i <- 1
  while i <= panjang(s) - 2 do
    if s[i] == 's' and s[i+1] == 't' and s[i+2] == 'd' then
      jumlah <- jumlah + 1
    endif
  endwhile
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with a while loop but didn't include the increment statement (i = i + 1) because they believe the while loop will only execute once. From their perspective, the while loop checks the condition and runs the body once, so there's no need to increment i - they think it will just check position 0 once and return. In reality, this creates an infinite loop because i never changes and the condition remains true indefinitely. The student genuinely believes this will work because they think while loops behave like if statements (execute once when condition is true).
